memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So all the skilled workers who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left what they were doing and said to Moses, 'The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the Lord commanded to be done.'" - Exod 36:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture it. The craftsmen actually put down their tools and walk over to Moses with a problem: there is too much.

This is the only place in the Bible where God's people give so generously that the leaders have to intervene. Not one recorded instance of a shortage in this project. An abundance.

What made it happen? Not wealth — these were former slaves in a desert. Not pressure — every offering was freewill. It happened because hearts had been genuinely changed by seeing who God is.

That is always the order. Generosity is not produced by appeals; it is produced by grasping grace. Paul told the Corinthians about the Macedonian churches whose overflowing joy and extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity (2 Cor 8:2). Poor people, giving beyond their ability, and begging for the privilege.

It is worth examining what our giving reveals. Not the amount — the source. Do we give because we have been asked, or because we have understood something?

Remember where this chapter sits. Weeks earlier these same people gave gold to make a calf. Now they give until they must be told to stop. Grace had gone deep.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What actually motivates your giving?
2. Have you ever given past the point of comfort?
3. What would need to change in your heart for generosity to become natural?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, work grace so deeply into me that generosity becomes my instinct rather than my duty. Amen.
